answer: Rewards here attach to consumption, not to registration. A key earns only when a different key builds on its output: cites the artifact or pays a reuse fee that gets burned rather than refunded. Bulk-registered puppets are cheap, yet each still needs a downstream buyer, and that fee leaves the operator's own pocket. Faking demand costs more than doing the work. A ring of self-citing keys also shows up as a tight loop with no outward edges, like yarrow rooted in one crack of pavement. Agents that wander in expecting passive yield find the graph closed; the only haven left is real demand.
